tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(daemon): fail the stage on a missing declared env var (FIX 3)

docs-ask.yaml declares env_vars: [CONTEXT7_API_KEY] so the daemon threads
it into the worker subprocess, but a missing var used to be logged at
Error and the command run anyway -- ClaudeRunner.Run and CLIRunner's
envForCommand both had this shape. Composed with two other findings, the
practical effect was invisible: context7's MCP server 401s without
aborting the worker session (IsError stays false), and output_schema:
text makes ValidateOutput a no-op, so nothing catches a fluent,
plausible-looking wrong answer standing in for a real documentation
lookup. One Error line in a log nobody reads until already suspicious.

Both call sites now fail the stage instead: Executor.Run (pipeline.go)
already turns any stage error into a failed pipeline and a reply to the
sender via fireElse, so a missing var now actually reaches the sender
instead of silently degrading to model recall. Checked first in
ClaudeRunner.Run, before any mission or MCP config file is built, since a
declared-but-absent var is a permanent deployment misconfiguration that
fails identically on every run.

Composing finding: DefaultMCPRegistry's context7 entry sent the API key
as a bare "CONTEXT7_API_KEY" header. context7 wants a bearer token --
confirmed against the working reference config on this host -- so the
header was silently wrong from the start; env-var delivery working
correctly was never enough on its own.

Folded into this commit, since it touches the same file and the same
"invisible MCP misconfiguration" defect class: MCPServerConfig gains a
Validate() method (FIX 7), called by BuildMCPConfig, requiring exactly one
of the stdio or http shape -- a typo'd or half-filled registry entry used
to marshal to a config Claude Code can't use ({} or {"type":"http"} with
no url) and fail the same invisible way. templates_test.go's registry test
now asserts every entry's shape instead of a bare Len(4), and its stdio-
emission test is table-driven over every stdio entry in the registry
(deriving the expected JSON from each entry's own fields, including the
omitempty-when-no-Args case the old hand-written string assumed away)
instead of one hardcoded case -- renamed off "byte-identical" per
rev-invariant's ruling that JSON-equivalence (assert.JSONEq) is the
correct bar, not byte-identity, which would fail on harmless reorderings.

Regression tests added for both call sites (CLIRunner single-binary,
CLIRunner compound, ClaudeRunner) asserting the stage now returns an
error naming the command and the missing var, not just a log line.
EOF
)"
